# CircuitSight — Dataset Card (current features)

*Generated by [src/CircuitSight_dataset_generation.ipynb](../src/CircuitSight_dataset_generation.ipynb). Last updated 2026-07-12. Every field below is procedurally generated — one structured spec deterministically drives BOTH the rendered image AND the solver-computed labels, so all labels are exact by construction (not AI-generated / not hallucinated).*

## Overview

| | |
|---|---|
| **Size** | `N_TRAIN = 10,000` records, split ~**9,500 train / ~500 val** (`VAL_FRAC = 0.05`) |
| **Unit** | one **schematic image** + one **question** + exact **gold labels** |
| **Task** | image → grounded, step-verified worked solution ending in a machine-readable `FINAL:` line |
| **Seed** | `SEED = 42` (fully reproducible) |
| **Image size** | matplotlib render, downscaled to ≤ `MAX_IMAGE_PX` at train time |

## Record schema (per record)

- `image` — path to the rendered schematic
- `question` — one natural-language question
- `family` — `dc_resistor` | `reactive` | `bridge`
- `question_type` / `quantity` — the quantity asked (see below)
- `value_mode` — `numeric` | `symbolic` | `mixed`
- `gold_components` — inventory by type (`voltage_source`, `resistor`, `capacitor`, `inductor`)
- `gold_boxes` — **bounding box per component**, `[x0,y0,x1,y1]` in **0–1000 normalized** coords
- `gold_topology` — series/parallel structure string (e.g. `R1 + (R2 || R3)`)
- `gold_answer` — `{quantity, target_id, value, unit, symbolic}` (or `null` for perception-only / abstain)
- `gold_values` — verifiable intermediates: `R_eq`, per-branch `branch_currents`, `I_total`
- `concepts` — the minimal solving concepts the problem needs (for concept-scoping checks)
- `abstain` — `true` when the asked value is deliberately illegible
- `target_output` — the full gold worked-solution text (what the model is trained to produce)

## 1. Circuit families (the complexity moat)

Mix of the non-abstain records:

| Family | Share | What it is | Solver |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dc_resistor** | ~60% | series/parallel resistor networks; up to **`MAX_LINKS=5` series links**, each up to a **`MAX_PARALLEL=4`-resistor** parallel block | series/parallel reduction |
| **reactive** | 25% (`REACTIVE_FRAC`) | resistor backbone + **one capacitor or inductor**, in series or as a shunt; solved at **steady-state (t→∞)** or **t=0** | steady/initial-value analysis |
| **bridge** | 15% (`BRIDGE_FRAC`) | **Wheatstone bridge** — *non-series-parallel*, the litmus case a generic model can't reduce | **nodal analysis (KCL/MNA)** |

This is the intended moat: complex topologies (4 branches / 3 resistors per branch, bridges) where generic VLMs fail.

## 2. Value modes (how values appear on the diagram)

DC-resistor records only; **bridge and reactive are always numeric**.

| Mode | Share (of DC) | Example | Answer form |
|---|---|---|---|
| **symbolic** | 45% (`SYMBOLIC_FRAC`) | `R1, R2, V` | algebraic expression (`R_eq = R1 + R2`), checked by sympy equivalence |
| **mixed** | 25% (`MIXED_FRAC`) | some numbers, some symbols | mostly algebraic |
| **numeric** | ~30% | `220Ω, 12V` | a number (needs arithmetic) |

Overall ~40% of the set is symbolic/mixed — this is the diagnostic that separates *reading + reasoning* from *arithmetic*.

## 3. Question types / quantities

`current`, `voltage`, `power`, `resistance` (R_eq), `charge`, `energy` — plus total-current and, for reactive circuits, quantities of the reactive element (`voltage`/`charge`/`energy` for a capacitor, `current`/`energy` for an inductor) at the given regime. Perception-only questions (topology / component inventory) are also supported.

## 4. Layout variety  *(NEW — `LAYOUT_VARIETY=True`)*

Circuits are drawn in **more than one geometry**, to break the spatial overfit that collapsed real-image grounding:

- **Ladder** — classic top-rail layout (source left, components on the top rail).
- **Rectangular loop** — perimeter walk: source on the left, components on the **top rail, a vertical right rail, and the bottom rail**. Chosen ~50% of the time for dc/reactive records.

Real AP diagrams routinely put resistors on vertical rails; this teaches the model to ground them anywhere, not just along a top rail.

## 5. Label-style variety  *(NEW — `LABEL_STYLE_VARIETY=True`)*

The **on-image** label varies per record, while the **model's output ids stay canonical** (`R1`, `V1`) — so it only ever trains the model to *read* real conventions, and the eval/gold are untouched:

- **Designator:** `R1` / `R₁` (unicode subscript) / `Resistor 1`
- **Source:** `V` / `ε` / `E` (EMF), optionally with the value
- Numeric labels always keep the value legible; styling only changes the designator.

## 6. Grounding / bounding boxes

Every component carries an axis-aligned gold box derived directly from its drawn position (matplotlib data-coords → normalized 0–1000), so boxes are exact for **any** layout. This is what powers the grounding metric (IoU ≥ 0.5 recall/precision).

## 7. Target output structure (the trained behavior)

Perception-before-answer, every claim grounded and every step checkable:

1. **Components** — inventory, each with its `<box>[…]</box>`
2. **Concepts used** — the minimal set (Ohm's law, series/parallel, steady-state, nodal analysis)
3. **Topology** — what's in series/parallel
4. **Solving** — reduce network → `R_eq` → total current → per-branch currents (bridges show KCL at each node)
5. **Verification** — a self-check
6. **`FINAL: {quantity, target_id, value, unit, abstain}`** — machine-readable

## 8. Honesty / abstention  *(`ABSTAIN_FRAC = 0.08`)*

~8% of records have a **deliberately illegible value** (the label is visually degraded); the correct behavior is to report `value: null` / `abstain: true` instead of fabricating a number. Scored as honest-abstention vs. fabrication.

## 9. Domain randomization (synthetic→real gap)

Applied **uniformly to every image** so no augmentation leaks a label:

| Op | Prob / range |
|---|---|
| page-tilt rotation (updates boxes) | `p=0.35`, ±`4.0°` |
| paper tint (off-white cast) | `p=0.50` |
| blur / noise / JPEG artifacts | `p=0.45 / 0.50 / 0.60` (JPEG quality 45–90) |
| graph-paper grid background | `p=0.12` |
| symbol style (zigzag vs box resistor), line width | random per image |
| horizontal / vertical flips | `p≈0.40 / 0.25` (source side / branch order swap) |

The small rotation transforms the gold boxes with the image, so grounding stays exact.

## 10. Diversity guard

`DEDUP_SKELETON_CAP = 400` — at most 400 circuits may share one structural skeleton, forcing structural variety. Layout + label variety multiply *visual* diversity within each skeleton (dedup is structural, so no dedup change was needed).

## 11. Optional features (currently OFF)

| Flag | Default | Effect when ON |
|---|---|---|
| `INCLUDE_PLAN` | **False** | append a machine-readable `PLAN` formula line for calculator tool-offload (abandoned — judge penalized it) |
| `INCLUDE_MISTAKES` | **False** | also emit `N_PAIRS=500` wrong-solution/correction preference pairs (for v2 DPO) |
| `INCLUDE_CONNECTIVITY` | **False** | add per-node connectivity (which components meet at each node) to gold + target |
| `USE_TEACHER` | **False** | polish worked-solution prose with a teacher LLM (offline by default) |
| `SAVE_TO_DRIVE` | **False** | also copy the dataset zip to Google Drive |

## Source-value pool & component values

Sources drawn from `SOURCE_VOLTS = [5,6,9,10,12,15,20,24] V`; resistors from a realistic E-series pool (`10Ω … 4.7kΩ`, 14 values); capacitors `1µF … 100µF` (7 values); inductors `1mH … 100mH` (7 values).
